Evaluated on CogVideoX-2B with 4,720 videos per configuration across all sixteen official VBench dimensions, BATMoS achieves the highest total score among the eight allocation policies and comes within 0.10 points of full classifier-free guidance using 20\% fewer branch evaluations. BATMoS also composes with feature reuse, reducing computation from 80 to 62 effective branch evaluations with a 0.11-point decrease in total score. These findings make temporal guidance allocation a practical mechanism for extracting more generation quality from a fixed inference budget.

papers.title: GauntletScore: Auditable Fact-Checking That Matches the Best Published Checkers on LLM-AggreFact
papers.summary: Checking whether a generated sentence is supported by its source document is a standard safeguard for AI-written text, and the strongest published checkers are single models. We describe GauntletScore, an evidence engine whose few rules and thresholds were set on the benchmark's development split. It puts typed questions to independent readers from different providers and records each answer as a measurement in an evidence ledger. It combines the measurements with a fixed Bayesian rule that counts a contradiction only when two readers agree. On the full LLM-AggreFact test split (29,320 claims across 11 datasets), following the leaderboard's approach, GauntletScore achieves 79.51 balanced accuracy, above every average published on the leaderboard as of 15 November 2026. That places it level with the best of them, nimble-v4-max (79.45 from its published dataset scores; the engine's 95% interval, 78.47 to 80.53, contains it). On the same claims it beats two of its three readers used alone (Readers A and B) by 1.66 and 2.17 points (95% intervals 0.80 to 2.53 and 1.29 to 3.06). Without AggreFact-CNN, described below, the leads are 0.90 and 1.32 and both intervals stay above zero. The engine also records the evidence behind every verdict, which a single model does not. Its largest margin is on full-length news articles checked against multi-sentence summaries (AggreFact-CNN), a format that resembles much regulated writing. There it scores 76.45, the best on the leaderboard, against 70.1 for the next best and 63.9 to 67.8 for the six systems with the highest averages. The test split was run once, on an engine frozen before the first test claim, under a stopping plan committed in advance. We release per-claim predictions and the scoring script.
papers.comment: 10 pages, 1 figure, 7 tables. Per-claim predictions and scoring script: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Gauntletscore/llm-aggrefact-predictions

papers.title: Causal Input--Output Modeling with Prior Information
papers.summary: We study the problem of inferring a causal input--output model from unpaired marginal observations and a given prior coupling. We formulate this problem using entropic causal optimal transport, which seeks a coupling that preserves the observed marginals, satisfies a one--sided causality constraint, and remains close to the prior. For Gaussian marginals and general quadratic costs, we prove that the optimal coupling is Gaussian and reduce the problem to a finite--dimensional optimization over covariance matrices. Using a Cholesky transformation to simplify the causality constraint, we derive a Lagrangian dual formulation and develop a block coordinate descent algorithm with explicit update formulas. We establish linear convergence of the algorithm, with explicit convergence rates, and prove stability of the optimal coupling under marginal covariance perturbations and derive a statistical error bound. We further show its equivalence to Sinkhorn iterations. Numerical experiments demonstrate the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithm and illustrate the predictive advantages of causal couplings.

papers.title: A mechanistic characterization of missingness at random
papers.summary: The missingness-at-random (MAR) assumption underlying many missing-data methods describes abstract statistical independences, whereas practitioners reason more naturally about the causal mechanisms that generate missingness. To bridge this gap, we provide a mechanistic characterization of MAR in terms of paths in a directed acyclic graph (DAG) modified to allow certain edges to cease to operate when an incomplete variable is missing, a property termed "context-specific causal irrelevance (CSCI)". Under a faithfulness condition, MAR holds if and only if the modified DAG contains no MAR-violating paths. Without CSCI, this condition reduces to a previously established d-separation condition, VMAR; thus, MAR without VMAR requires specific kinds of CSCI, as can occur with monotone dropout. These results shift the burden on investigators from passively invoking MAR to justifying, on substantive grounds, the specific mechanisms it requires. We then consider identification of a target law p(v) of variables V by a MAR-assuming analysis, e.g., multiple imputation, that includes complete auxiliary variables Z (variables not in V). Barring a perfect cancellation, such an analysis recovers p(v) if and only if MAR holds with respect to V and Z jointly. We show that if there exists any set of auxiliaries such that (V, Z) obeys MAR, then the complete candidate auxiliaries that are ancestors of the target variables or their missingness indicators form a sufficient set. Contrary to standard recommendations, not all candidate auxiliaries should be used: even complete auxiliaries can introduce MAR violations that would not otherwise occur. We illustrate these results with simulations and an analysis of sexual identity change in the Stockholm Public Health Cohort, where our results indicate that a candidate auxiliary, income, should be excluded; including it attenuated estimates toward the null.
papers.comment: 70 pages: 34-page main text followed by 36-page supplement

papers.title: Frame Based Inelasticity for Strength and Fracture in Anisotropic Media
papers.summary: A field theory is presented for predicting damage and fracture in brittle materials. Four concepts are used: a new nonlocal deformation gradient for dynamic stress analysis in anisotropic media, a new type of phase field coming from a constitutive law, the evolution of material displacement from Newton's second law, and a new incorporation of scaled strength surfaces into constitutive laws for predicting dynamic and quasi-static fracture patterns. The elastic softening is governed by the strain dynamics through the constitutive law and in this way we provide the two way coupling between strain and fracture. Simulations validating the approach for both dynamic and quasi-static fracture analysis are compared to experimental results and other simulation methods. The model is capable of predicting material strength in titania and the competition between strength and energy in soda lime glass and titana and captures dynamic crack branching in soda lime glass and concrete.

papers.title: SkillBuffBench: Measuring What Agent Skills Contribute across Harnesses, Models, Skill Access Modes and Memory
papers.summary: Agent Skills, file-based packages of procedural knowledge that a coding agent can discover and load on demand, are now shipped by every major agent harness, yet the evidence for how much they help comes almost entirely from settings in which the right Skill is hand-picked for the task and the agent starts from a blank slate. Neither holds in deployment, where an agent chooses from whatever library happens to be installed and frequently carries memory from earlier work. We present SkillBuffBench, a benchmark and paired evaluation protocol that treats Skill access as a three-level factor (no Skill, a curated Skill, and automatic invocation from an installed library), crosses it with memory (off and on), with four agent harnesses and with multiple models (the state-of-the-art proprietary models from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI, and the state-of-the-art open-weight models from Chinese providers), every model being run under every harness, and evaluates the result on research tasks contributed by domain experts together with the Skills they use, currently in materials science and biology, with the suite extended on a rolling basis. Every run is marked by a deterministic verifier; uncertainty is reported with a paired, task-level bootstrap; and cost, agent rounds and wall-clock time are reported alongside the score rather than folded into it. This version of the paper describes the design of the benchmark, its evaluation protocol and its current tasks and Skills. The evaluation is in progress: results will be added once the runs are complete, and the task suite, results and analysis will continue to be updated on a rolling basis.
papers.comment: 18 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables. Work in progress: benchmark design and protocol; results to be added in a later version

papers.title: An Explainable Agentic AI Framework for Distribution System Load Restoration
papers.summary: Distribution system load restoration is a sequential decision-making problem in which restoration actions must maximize served load, prioritize critical loads, and preserve power-flow feasibility. This paper proposes an explainable agentic artificial intelligence (AI) framework for distribution system load restoration. The proposed framework uses multiple large language model (LLM) agents for planner guidance, strategic plan generation, decision arbitration, memory-based feedback, and explanation generation. Unlike unconstrained LLM-based control, the proposed method restricts agent decisions to feasible restoration actions and evaluates all candidate plans using deterministic AC power-flow feasibility checks. The framework is evaluated on IEEE 33-bus and 69-bus distribution feeders, as well as a larger IEEE 118-bus test case, and compared against reinforcement learning and planning baselines. The results show that the proposed agentic framework achieves better restoration performance while producing structured explanations for operator-facing decision support. A direct comparison with a Single-LLM-Agent baseline further shows that the proposed multi-agent decomposition improves weighted restored load and critical-load recovery compared with a monolithic LLM decision structure.

papers.title: Theoretical Instability Models of Quasi-Periodic Eruptions
papers.summary: The nature of the Quasi-Periodic Eruptions (QPE) is still not firmly established while the phenomenon probes the innermost part of the accretion flow undergoing dramatic changes. In this chapter we review the possibility that the observed rapid variability is caused by the accretion disk instability. We summarise the defining observational properties of QPE sources: time scales of recurrence, the amplitudes of soft X-ray flares, high coherence over many cycles, and comparatively modest time-averaged luminosities. We then translate these into constraints on the characteristic radius, accretion rate, and energy reservoir of the inner disk. We review the main classes of disk instabilities relevant to supermassive black holes: radiation pressure induced thermal/viscous limit cycles, magnetically mediated inner disk transitions, and coupling to disk winds that can produce the oscillatory behavior. For each scenario we discuss the required parameter space (black hole mass, Eddington ratio, viscosity prescription, and truncation radius), the predicted spectral and timing signatures, and the degree of fine tuning needed to reproduce the observed duty cycles and flare morphologies. We highlight key tensions, including the extremely soft spectra, short recurrence times compared with standard viscous times at tens of gravitational radii, and the weak or absent contemporaneous optical/UV variability in several systems. Finally, we outline observational tests that may help distinguish between instability driven and geometrical or orbital models: phase resolved spectroscopy to track the temperature evolution, searches for hysteresis in hardness-intensity diagrams, reverberation and absorption variability tied to winds, and long baseline monitoring to measure drift in period and energy output.
papers.comment: 25 pages; Invited review chapter for the book "Mysterious Repeating Signals from Centers of Galaxies" (Eds. Dheeraj Pasham, Eric Coughlin, Riccardo Arcodia, Petra Sukova, Itai Linial, Springer Singapore, expected in 2027). After first referee report, comments welcome

papers.title: Generalized Schrieffer-Wolff transformation
papers.summary: The Schrieffer-Wolff transformation (SWT) is a cornerstone of effective-Hamiltonian theory. However, the SWT is predominantly used for weak-coupling problems, while a systematic counterpart for strongly coupled regimes remains largely unexplored. A general closed-form SWT generator and a clear physical principle for gauge fixing remain elusive, obscuring the transformation's underlying structure. We introduce the dual SWT to deal with the strong-coupling problems. The generalized SWT (gSWT) is formulated for any Hermitian operator and block partition. We establish the geodesic principle for its canonical gauge. Furthermore, we derive an exact closed-form solution of the gSWT generator at every order as a finite nested-commutator sum whose only input is the active gap set. Both the geometric and algebraic aspects of the SWT physics are revealed. The gSWT framework is illustrated in two quantum many-body models, the collective spin model and the transverse-field Ising model.

papers.title: Weight-Space Programming for Materials Science
papers.summary: A materials discovery campaign often begins with almost no measurements of the property it is searching for, and the models that rank candidates or screen the output of a generator then have to be built from those first few labels. Following recent work on weight-space programming, in which a language model writes the weights of a small network directly as text, we show that a general-purpose model, given the task in words, the names of the inputs and a network of 16 hidden units with every weight set to zero, can provide this starting point by filling in all of the weights from what it has learned about materials. With no labels, the networks of the strongest model rank experimental alloys at Spearman co-efficient = 0.64 to 0.79, where the best of five simple descriptors reaches 0.47 to 0.62. They rank the bulk modulus of crystals added during generative discovery loops at 0.95, where the inverse volume per atom reaches 0.89, and 35 phase-equilibrium targets computed with Thermo-Calc at a mean of 0.67, close to the 0.70 of an extrapolation from calculated binary and ternary data. As the prior mean of a Gaussian process they raise the ranking at five labels from 0.35 to 0.69 on alloys and from 0.15 to 0.95 on crystals, and they lower the regret of Bayesian optimization significantly on 4 of 5 experimental tasks and on 13 to 16 of 33 computed targets, depending on how multiple tests are corrected, without raising it significantly on any. The same networks also serve as the mean of a Bayesian neural network and as a screen for the samples of two crystal generators, where they do as well as standard models trained on 400 labeled structures. The gain is confined to the first tens of labels and to targets that no rule or sub-system extrapolation already ranks.

papers.title: PS-HalluBench: Taxonomy-Driven Benchmarking of LLM Hallucinations in Power Systems
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored for power-system applications, yet their reliability in engineering analysis remains uncertain. We introduce PS-HalluBench, a manually constructed benchmark of 200 questions that evaluates hallucination-related failures across five power-system task categories: numerical reasoning, network topology, constraint verification, false-premise acceptance, and abstention. We evaluate ten LLMs over the benchmark, yielding 39.35\% overall correctness, with constraint verification achieving only 21.75\%, and highlighting persistent difficulties in engineering reasoning. We further investigate engineering-grounded reasoning through numerical solver support and verified network information both of which show significant performance improvement. The findings reveal important limitations of standalone LLM reasoning and motivate integrating LLMs with verified engineering tools for reliable power-system analysis.

papers.title: Locally Linear Generalized Single Index Regression
papers.summary: In this work we propose and analyze a procedure for estimating a generalized single-index regression model. This generalized single-index regression framework models the conditional mean of the responses $Y$ as a function of the covariates $X$ where the mapping is assumed to have the form $f \circ g$, where $g$ is $β$-Hölder with $β\geq 2$ and $f$ can be a discontinuous function of bounded variation. We propose a general procedure that operates under minimal assumptions about the distribution of covariates $X$, requiring only boundedness, sufficient smoothness and absolute continuity with respect to Lebesgue. Our procedure jointly estimates the gradient vector $\hat v(x) \approx \nabla g(x)$ and the conditional mean $μ(x) = f(g(x))$ by solving a localized weighted linear least squares problem. We derive central limit theorems for gradient vector estimates $\hat{v}_x$ and regression estimates $\hatμ(x)$, and we derive rates of convergence for our approach, illustrating that it indeed achieves a stochastic convergence rate matching the minimax mean squared error rate when $β= 2$ and $f$ has a locally Lipschitz derivative. Unlike prior approaches our velocity estimation results accommodate link functions in the local bounded-variation class, allowing for nonsmooth and even discontinuous links while retaining consistency and asymptotic normality at almost every inference point. Finally, we instantiate this model in the situation where $g = Π$ is a closest point projection onto a compact and regular embedded $C^3$ curve $γ$, a setting recently studied in the literature. We also supplement our theoretical results with experiments on real and synthetic data to demonstrate the utility of our procedure.

papers.title: DiagTrace: An Interactive Benchmark for Clinical Decision Making
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance on medical question answering and diagnostic reasoning benchmarks. However, existing evaluations typically provide all patient information upfront and assess only the final diagnosis or rationale. This setup ignores the need to acquire diagnostic evidence incrementally from incomplete information in real-world diagnosis. To bridge this gap, we introduce DiagTrace, a source-grounded benchmark for evaluating whether LLMs can reconstruct the documented diagnostic trajectory through interactive information seeking. Each benchmark instance is built from a PubMed Central case report and includes an initial presentation, an event bank, a clinical course, and diagnostic references. DiagTrace contains 510 cases across eight specialties, with 225 used to evaluate four LLMs on clinical-course alignment, interaction quality, and efficiency. Results reveal trade-offs in coverage, source-consistent ordering, and turn use.

papers.title: Stokes flow in a wedge with a moving contact point: well-posedness with a fixed contact angle and Navier slip
papers.summary: We study 2D Stokes flow in a wedge-like region bounded by a solid substrate with Navier slip and by a free surface driven by surface tension. The two meet at a moving contact point with a fixed contact angle. This is the model of a moving contact line at scales below the slip length, in its simplest setting. The slip length is the only length scale, and nothing is prescribed at the contact point beyond the angle: no relaxation law for the angle, and no contact-point dissipation. Slip removes the paradox found by Huh and Scriven, the infinite dissipation at a contact line that moves without slip, but in this model a weaker singularity remains. We give, to our knowledge, the first rigorous characterisation of this singularity for solutions of the free-boundary problem near the stationary state. For small contact angles and small initial data satisfying two compatibility conditions, we prove local existence, uniqueness and Lipschitz dependence on the data. The compatibility conditions are the price of the fixed angle for solutions regular in time up to the initial time. Rather than hiding the singularity, the solution class carries it explicitly in corner expansions. The velocity is continuous up to the contact point. The pressure has a logarithmic singularity, the slip-regularised version of that of Huh and Scriven. Its coefficient is proportional to the contact-point velocity. The slope of the free boundary has a corresponding logarithmic correction, the slip-scale counterpart of the Cox-Voinov relation. The linearised problem combines terms of different scaling, which prevents a direct treatment by the Mellin transform. We solve it by a Lax-Milgram argument, and an auxiliary test function problem shows that the variational solution satisfies the equations. Explicit Mellin representations then yield the corner expansions, and the nonlinear problem is solved by a contraction argument.

papers.title: The interplay between ionized and warm molecular gas in the turbulent intragroup medium of Stephan's Quintet
papers.summary: Using JWST MIRI spectroscopy, we explore the multi-phase intergalactic gas in the hot halo of the Stephan's Quintet compact group. Unlike the coolest H2 emission, which commonly shows double- peaked profiles corresponding to the velocity of the intruder and the intragroup gas, the ionized Neon emission-lines are often systematically shifted redwards in radial velocity away from the lowest H2 peak, and into the region corresponding to gas decelerated by the collision of the intruder galaxy with intragroup gas. The majority of the brightest clumps of ionized gas are spatially correlated with the brightest H2 clumps, suggesting they are coherent structures caught up in the opposing gas flows. Gas that is progressively heated, is shifted in velocity further from the velocity of the coldest H2 peaks. Larger and larger shifts in velocity are seen as one progresses from cool to warm molecular hydrogen, to lower-excitation (Neon lines) ionized and strongly shocked heated ionized gas (gas-phase Iron). The majority of the ionized Neon in the intergalactic medium is consistent with excitation in low-velocity shocks. We suggest that this behavior is the result of gas of progressively lower densities being shocked and accelerated by the interaction of pre-existing clouds with a hot flow created by the blast-wave from the collision between the intruder and the intragroup gas. One exception is the extragalactic star forming region, SQ-A, which shows higher-excitation ionized emission lines consistent with heating from a young starburst, consistent with previous photometry of young star clusters in the region.
papers.comment: 21 pages, 7 figures: Accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal, November 2026

papers.title: Supporting Researcher Control in AI-Assisted Social Media Analysis: A Mixed-Methods Study of AI4OSN
papers.summary: High-quality annotated datasets are critical for advancing computational social science (CSS) research, yet collecting, curating, and analyzing large-scale data from dynamic sources such as online social networks (OSNs) remains a persistent bottleneck. Researchers must also translate substantive questions into queries, relevance criteria, and defensible interpretations. Large language models (LLMs) can assist, but they can also obscure the judgments, potentially reducing researcher oversight and critical evaluation. We present AI4OSN, a mixed-initiative platform that keeps researchers in control of data collection, relevance labeling, and sensemaking while making AI assistance available as an inspectable advisory resource. In a systematic user study (N=18) using X/Twitter data, participants reported above-benchmark perceived usability (mean SUS score of 79.7), increased confidence in LLM-assisted annotation and analysis tasks, and low cognitive workload during AI-supported sensemaking. Notably, novice participants showed descriptively greater alignment and higher reported agreement with AI output than experienced participants, underscoring the need to support differentiated verification practices across expertise levels. Overall, this work contributes both a human-centered system for social data analysis and empirical insights into how AI-assisted interfaces shape researcher behavior, trust, and decision-making. Our findings highlight design opportunities and tensions in building accessible, transparent, and agentic AI systems for social media and web research.

papers.title: Where Should the Lamp Go? Ambient-Aware Lamp Placement for Portraits
papers.summary: Portraits shape first impressions, and lighting is an important factor. Prior work, such as lighting estimation and portrait relighting, edits lighting after capture but does not guide where to place a light before the shot. This leaves an open question: where should a light go to best light a face? Therefore, we propose LightMatch, a preference-grounded inverse lighting framework that disentangles the controllable light from ambient illumination and optimizes its placement. We first learn a Bradley-Terry quality model from pairwise human judgments. A perception head then regresses spherical-harmonic lighting from frozen self-supervised features via cross-attention. Finally, a placement solver isolates the light via spherical-harmonic linearity and optimizes its reachable position. On held-out environments, LightMatch attains 87.8% of the oracle improvement, outperforming the conventional solver that ignores ambient light by a relative 28.4% and the same pipeline with the widely used DPR estimator by a relative 70.5%. It reaches 73.2% on real OLAT faces of unseen identities and, on our real captures, cuts lamp-direction error by 37.7%.

papers.title: VLA Observations of the Ionized Jet IRAS 16562-3959
papers.summary: We present new high-resolution, high-sensitivity Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) A-configuration observations of the high-mass protostellar jet system IRAS 16562-3959 at 3.1 and 6.1 GHz. Our images resolve the five previously known jet components (OE, IE, C, IW, OW) into 21 distinct knots and sub-components, and reveal a new off-axis source, MW. Based on the dynamical timescales from previous works ($τ_{jet} \approx 620$ yr), the spacing and structure of the knots suggest episodic accretion with a mean interval between ejections of $\sim$32 yr. We find that source MW has a substantial increase in peak brightness relative to its marginal detections in previous observations. MW exhibits a spectral index of $α\approx -0.7$, characteristic of synchrotron emission from shock-accelerated relativistic electrons. Equipartition analysis yields a minimum-energy magnetic field strength $B_{me} \approx 0.4$ mG, and a minimum total energy $E_{me} \approx 4.4 \times 10^{42}$ erg. Archival 2MASS Ks data imply a total outflow dynamical age of $\sim$1400 yr, and together with a HST [FeII] 1.64 $μ$m map, the NIR data indicate that the fast jet is embedded in a wide-angle wind with a $\sim 36^\circ$ opening angle.
papers.comment: 18 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal on Nov 10, 2026

papers.title: DreamFAR: Real-Time and Long-Horizon Interaction with Diverse Objects
papers.summary: World models have shown great potential in serving as a simulator for robot manipulation. However, existing models are either fit to a single environment or lack ability to simulate long-horizon contact-rich events. We present DreamFAR, a world model whose dynamics model is trained from scratch on a large robot-native teleoperation dataset, with no internet-video pretraining. We present an architecture and learning recipe designed for training on robot-native data. DreamFAR is significantly smaller than the high-performance video generation models, yet shows better understanding of contact and causality, and runs 10 FPS on a commercial GPU. Experimentally, DreamFAR significantly outperforms existing models in predicting the long-horizon future. We further demonstrate various applications where DreamFAR can be used, including policy evaluation and mixed-data co-training. Project page: https://www.yimingdou.com/DreamFAR/

papers.title: Transient Synchronization and Entanglement through Shared Dissipation in Circuit QED
papers.summary: We propose a superconducting circuit in which two resonators couple through DC-biased SQUIDs to a common lossy auxiliary mode. Adiabatic elimination yields collective damping and correlated noise with an overlap $ξ$ whose magnitude is tuned by the flux biases and whose sign follows the relative sign of the couplings. The full three-mode dynamics confirm this reduced description. For detuned resonators, we derive the exceptional-point condition, above which the mean amplitudes lock to a common frequency. For resonant modes, unequal collective decay produces transient synchronization, antiphase or in phase depending on the relative sign of the couplings, with an analytical synchronization time set by the collective decay splitting and the initial mean amplitudes. For initially separable squeezed states, the same relaxation converts local squeezing into transient entanglement, quantified by logarithmic negativity. We obtain closed-form expressions for the squeezing threshold above which entanglement appears and for the time at which it disappears. Thermal noise suppresses entanglement without changing the mean-amplitude synchronization time at fixed parameters. For realistic circuit parameters, these effects occur within a few hundred nanoseconds and are accessible through output-field measurements. A single tunable shared channel thus produces an exceptional point, transient synchronization, and transient entanglement, and provides a controllable source of correlated noise for superconducting circuits.

papers.title: Fundamental physics with quantum sensors in space
papers.summary: Quantum sensors such as atomic clocks, atom interferometers, and atomic magnetometers can be used as sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model. Space offers microgravity, long baselines, low environmental noise, access to varying gravitational potentials, and unique opportunities involving the Sun, Moon, planets, and asteroids. These proceedings of the Aspen Center for Physics workshop on "Fundamental physics in space with quantum sensors," held February 22-27, 2026, summarize the scientific case, current capabilities, and space mission concepts for investigating dark matter, testing general relativity, and detecting gravitational waves in frequency bands inaccessible from the ground.

papers.title: Beyond Appearance: Where Forest Visual Place Recognition Actually Fails
papers.summary: Visual place recognition (VPR) in forest environments remains challenging because repetitive vegetation, and changes in illumination, season, and viewpoint can make distinct places appear similar and revisited places appear substantially different. In this paper, we investigate whether temporal, linguistic, structural, and geometric context can improve on an appearance-only descriptor, and what limits each representation when it does not. Using MegaLoc as the appearance-based baseline on the WildCross benchmark, we evaluate score-space and descriptor-space sequence matching, vision-language captions and reranking, scene-graph representations, and depth-derived stem graphs across same-direction revisits, extended routes, and reverse traversals. On a same-direction revisit, both sequence matching strategies reach similar Recall@1 (94.1% vs. 91.5%), but recall at 100% precision rises from 50.9% (single-frame MegaLoc) to 71.6% in score space and falls to 36.5% in descriptor space. The remaining context representations provide no consistent improvement over the appearance-based baseline. Same-place captions show limited place-specific discrimination, reranking is constrained by the initial candidate shortlist, and stem-graph matching remains weak even with LiDAR depth.
papers.comment: 10 pages, 6 figures, accepted to the Australasian Conference on Robotics and Automation (ACRA)

papers.title: Deciding Without Pointing: A Case Study of Whether a Decision Model Localizes the Anomalies It Detects
papers.summary: Decision models can answer a typed question about an image with a probability per option, without generating text. In our case study of Clef-flash (post-trained Qwen3.5-9B backbone) on industrial inspection benchmarks, we ask whether it localizes the anomalies it detects. We obtained uneven results with zero-shot detection: per-category image AUROC 0.924 on MVTec AD and 0.668 on MVTec AD 2. On the former, the decision head's routing attention produces 0.391 mean per-image pixel AUROC, and hiding the image tokens from it leaves detection unchanged. The multimodal LLM's backbone attention does point at the defect, however it falls below a center prior when we change question. It falls below chance if we remove textual context in the question, partly due to backbone attention leaving the object, while the head's map hardly changes. The backbone's states carry the location when probed with normal images, on the test-split images, however, the decision depends on the defect region. A larger model, Clef, that comes with a post-trained Qwen3.8-27B backbone, gives no useful map in the decision head either. We found that it's possible to recover anomaly location by asking question specifically on an image region, retraining the head or reading the backbone, but none matches dedicated few-shot localizers.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, 14 tables. Preprint of the technical part of an MSc thesis (Politecnico di Milano). Code and pre-registrations are held privately until venue submission

papers.title: An alternate proof of the QMA lower bound for set-size estimation
papers.summary: In the set-size estimation query task, a query algorithm decides whether an $N$-bit input has Hamming weight $\ge B$ or $\le A$ (with $\ge B$ as the yes instances and $\le A$ as the no instances). When $B = 2A$, this is sometimes called approximate counting. The query complexity for this problem with a quantum witness (i.e., $\mathsf{QMA}$ query bounds) was resolved by Aaronson, Kothari, Kretschmer, and Thaler (CCC 2020) and proved using Laurent polynomials. Here we give a morally similar but distinct proof of the lower bound using the polynomial method.

papers.title: DEFTS: Data-Efficient, Training-Free Few-Shot Learning for CLIP in the Text Subspace
papers.summary: Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) achieves impressive zero-shot image classification performance by comparing image embeddings against class-specific text embeddings. While recent few-shot methods leverage labeled training samples to improve upon this zero-shot baseline, they often predominantly rely on image embeddings and underutilize the semantic structure of the text embeddings. In this paper, we introduce DEFTS, a data-efficient, training-free few-shot classification method strictly in the text subspace. We first demonstrate empirically that while raw text embeddings can be suboptimal as direct classifiers, the linear subspace they span remains highly discriminative. DEFTS therefore proposes to reduce the image-text modality gap by projecting estimated image prototypes directly into this subspace. Importantly, by expressing these prototypes as linear combinations of text embeddings, DEFTS reduces a high-dimensional estimation problem to the derivation of just a few coefficients. These coefficients are then computed via a Bayesian posterior mean, using a prior naturally centered on the original text embedding coordinates. Extensive experiments across 12 image classification benchmarks demonstrate that DEFTS significantly improves upon existing training-free methods.

papers.title: Accelerating auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo with mixed-precision random propagators
papers.summary: We develop an algorithm to propagate auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) wavefunctions in mixed precision. We target NVIDIA Tensor Cores using the TensorFloat-32 (TF32) format. We approximate each full-precision array by a TF32 leading term and a TF32 residual, and each full-precision matrix product by three TF32 products accumulated in full precision. Benchmarks on hydrogen chains show that mixed-precision propagation is consistently faster than double-precision GPU propagation, with an increasing advantage as the system size grows. The resulting local-energy deviations remain small over the propagation windows considered here. These results identify the stochastic two-body propagator as a particularly effective target for reduced precision, while our method allows higher precision to be retained for accuracy-sensitive operations. Hence, our algorithm provides a practical way to speed up AFQMC calculations and demonstrates where reduced precision can be applied without adverse effects on the method's accuracy.

papers.title: High-Order Regularization for Singular and Nearly Singular Laplace and Stokes Layer Potentials in Two Dimensions
papers.summary: Layer potentials represent the solutions of many elliptic boundary value problems, but their kernels have the singularity of the fundamental solution, so standard quadrature loses accuracy at targets on or near the boundary. In two dimensions, Gaussian regularization of the logarithmic kernel gives a smooth kernel involving the exponential integral $E_1$, but for the single layer its regularization error is only first order in the smoothing radius $δ$. We construct modified kernels for two-dimensional Laplace and Stokes single- and double-layer potentials that achieve regularization error $O(δ^p)$, $p=3,5,7$, uniformly for targets on and near the curve. The resulting method is both high-order accurate and easy to implement: the integrals are evaluated directly by the periodic trapezoidal rule on a single fixed set of boundary nodes for all targets. Choosing $δ=c h^q$ with $q<1$, where $h$ is the node spacing, keeps the discretization error smaller than the regularization error as $h\to0$, and numerical experiments confirm the predicted $O(h^{pq})$ convergence. Finally, we combine the near-curve evaluation with a fast Poisson solver to compute the potentials on the entire Cartesian grid.
papers.comment: 36 pages, 11 figures; code and data available at https://github.com/han-zhou-math/high-order-reg-2d

papers.title: Deep Learning Models for Fractional Option Pricing
papers.summary: This paper investigates whether neural networks can infer fractional option prices and the Hurst parameter directly from sequences of fractional Gaussian returns, without separately estimating the latent parameters for each new sequence. Feedforward neural networks (FNNs) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks are trained to jointly predict European call prices, put prices, and the Hurst parameter from 252-return sequences. A controlled simulation varies the total sample size from 5,000 to 500,000 sequences and evaluates point prediction, empirical residual-based prediction intervals, and computational performance. The neural-network models are also compared on a common simulated test set with Bayesian joint estimation and exact Gaussian maximum likelihood estimation. In that four-method comparison, the LSTM achieves the lowest Hurst-parameter root mean squared error (0.033) and option-price root mean squared error (1.305). After training, neural-network predictions are substantially faster than repeated parameter estimation, although the methods quantify uncertainty in different ways. Applications to five financial return series illustrate differences between data-driven and model-based fractional price estimates. The results support sequence-based learning as a computationally efficient complement to statistical inference under the assumed fractional model; they do not establish out-of-distribution accuracy or accuracy against observed traded-option prices.

papers.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning with Hard Constraints: Policy Gradient Methods with Intersample Guarantees
papers.summary: We develop a policy-gradient (PG) reinforcement learning (RL) framework with hard inter-sample control barrier function (CBF)-based safety constraints for nonlinear sampled-data systems. We first design a class of stochastic policies with support truncated to sampling-period-dependent safe control sets, that guarantee safety-by-construction at sampling instants. We then propose a model-free PG algorithm that searches over the class of safe-by-design policies and establish sufficient conditions on sampling-period such that any action sampled from safe control sets remains safe throughout the sampling interval, providing inter-sample guarantees. We further establish finite-time convergence and sample complexity guarantees for the proposed PG algorithm and characterize its global optimality under gradient dominance. Finally, we illustrate inter-sample safety guarantees on a safe quadrotor navigation environment.

papers.title: Unveiling the infrared excess of SIPS J2045-6332 II: SPHEREx spectral decomposition supports a young unresolved binary interpretation
papers.summary: SIPS J2045-6332 is an unusual low-mass object previously identified by its infrared excess and possible signatures of youth and unresolved multiplicity. Earlier work suggested that it is relatively young and may host a mid-L companion. Here we reassess the system using low-resolution 0.75-5 micron spectroscopy from SPHEREx. We perform single- and binary-template spectral decomposition with field-gravity and intermediate-gravity (beta) templates spanning M8-L4. Binary-template models consistently outperform single-template models, most strongly for the beta templates. The preferred solution, an L0beta + L1beta combination (reduced chi^2 = 10.72), best matches the combined-light spectrum, although M9beta + L1beta and M9beta + L2beta give comparably good fits. Combining bolometric luminosities from gravity-dependent bolometric corrections (log L/Lsun = -3.42 +/- 0.08 and -3.85 +/- 0.09) with the Sonora evolutionary models, we estimate component masses of ~0.015 and ~0.011 Msun at 25 Myr and >~0.043-0.046 and ~0.038-0.043 Msun at 200-250 Myr for the primary and secondary (primary values are lower limits), implying a mass ratio q <~ 0.7-0.9, i.e. a companion of comparable but not necessarily equal mass. These results independently reinforce previous interpretations that SIPS J2045-6332 is a relatively young unresolved binary, and demonstrate the capability of SPHEREx spectroscopy to characterise young low-mass binaries through spectral decomposition.

papers.title: First-Order Model-Free Policy Gradient for Undiscounted LQR with Global Optimality and Convergence Guarantees
papers.summary: We provide a first-order model-free policy gradient (PG) framework for learning undiscounted infinite-horizon linear quadratic regulator (LQR) policies with global optimality and convergence guarantees. We first construct a stochastic wrapper policy class parameterized by the LQR gain to enable exploration around a deterministic linear control law. We analyze the additional cost induced by exploration over infinite-horizon, and establish a weak gradient dominance condition that characterizes global optimality under exploration. We then construct a model-free first-order PG algorithm using sampled trajectory information, without identifying the dynamics or approximating a value function. Finally, we establish finite-time convergence guarantees, providing the sufficient number of samples required for near-global optimality with our proposed PG algorithms.

papers.title: Large Language Models as Nonlinear Dynamical Systems: The Three Clocks of Depth, Training, and Generation
papers.summary: Language models are dynamical systems. A transformer is iterated over its layers, over the steps of its training and over the tokens it generates, and on each of these three clocks it shows behavior that nonlinear dynamics has studied for a century: fixed points, bifurcations, synchronization, chaos and noise-driven escape from potential wells. The two communities rarely meet, so this behavior is often rediscovered under new names. We build a bridge between them. To describe, we condense about 200 papers into the Three-Clock Dictionary, which maps fifteen concepts of nonlinear dynamics onto each clock and marks every correspondence as proved, measured or conjectured, and we show each concept in a mechanical system and in a language model side by side. To explain, we derive reduced-order models: the softmax is a Boltzmann distribution, gradient descent an Euler step on a nonlinear spring, a loss spike a ball thrown out of a stiff valley, attention on the circle a Kuramoto model, and a repetition loop a well that deepens while it is occupied. We then test these explanations on open language models, on a laptop CPU. Escape from repetition loops in GPT-2 and Pythia follows the Arrhenius law with the logit gap as the barrier, and the barrier deepens and then saturates, so the temperature needed to leave a loop falls like $1/\ln N$ with the generation length $N$ and rises with model size. Coherent text lives in a narrow window of temperatures, which a small reasoning model shares at its recommended temperature. Training makes each Pythia layer more expansive, and a small transformer trains at a multi-mode edge of stability. The third step, solving problems of language models, is still ahead: controllers derived from the escape analysis remove loops but do not yet beat the best fixed temperature. We state twelve open problems where nonlinear dynamics could get there.

papers.title: Emerging Vertical Power Delivery in AI Data Centers: Challenges and Solutions
papers.summary: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads is increasing power demand in AI data centers, and processor current is projected to reach 2000 A and beyond. This trend is exposing the limitations of lateral power delivery (LPD) to processors and has motivated growing interest in vertical power delivery (VPD). This paper reviews the power delivery network (PDN) of AI data centers and the upcoming transition from LPD to VPD. First, the 800 VDC power delivery architecture, the impedance behavior of the PDN, and the limitations of LPD are discussed. Then, VPD implementation approaches, reported converter designs, and packaging technologies are examined, together with integrated voltage regulators (IVRs) and embedded passive components. In addition, power integrity simulations are presented to compare regulator and plane positions, from which a set of PDN design guidelines is derived. The results show that moving a voltage regulator module (VRM) from 50 mm away to directly below the die reduces the loop inductance by nearly half. In a complete PDN, this relocation lowers the low-frequency anti-resonant peak, whereas the mid- and high-frequency impedance depends on the decoupling stages and the position of the power and ground planes. This paper also shows that achieving practical VPD remains closely tied to challenges such as regulator height, passive-component embedding, and thermal management.
papers.comment: 29 pages, 24 figures. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

papers.title: Who Gets the Grid Capacity? Allocating Dynamic Access Among Multiple Virtual Power Plants
papers.summary: Virtual power plants (VPPs) trade in the same wholesale market and share distribution lines and transformers, and uncoordinated, profit-maximizing VPPs can push a shared transformer past its thermal limit or drive a feeder voltage out of band. The utility, which only observes the front-of-the-meter net injection at each bus, must keep the network safe from that net injection alone. We allocate a 24-hour active and reactive operating envelope to each VPP by a Benders decomposition: the utility sets a trial envelope, each VPP solves its private convex portfolio problem, and the returned value and dual gradient become supporting cuts that rebuild its value function while its schedule, state, and cost stay private. The envelope carries the transformer's thermal state across hours, bounds a joint conditional value-at-risk over forecast uncertainty, and is re-optimized each hour with the current hour committed. On a reduced IEEE-13 feeder with real load and prices, an active-power-only implementation lowers the transformer's peak-temperature CVaR from 254 to 97\,$^\circ$C at a 28\% value give-up and holds the transformer below its limit where nameplate access breaches it.

papers.title: Modeling Document and Section Hierarchies in Embedding Space
papers.summary: Embedded topic models integrate word embeddings into the topic generation process, producing coherent topics and robust performance on large vocabularies. However, each document is represented by a single topic distribution, ignoring its internal structure. Many real world collections, including legal documents, company and government reports, and online discussion forums, exhibit hierarchical organization in which documents consist of multiple sections that often address distinct subtopics. We introduce the Hierarchical Embedded Topic Model (hETM), a structured topic model that couples the topic distribution of a document and those of its sections through a hierarchical prior in the embedding space. We derive an amortized variational inference procedure for hETM and evaluate it on structured collections from each of these domains. Experimental results show that hETM achieves the lowest or near-lowest held-out perplexity among flat and hierarchical topic model baselines, along with comparable or higher topic quality. It also performs strongly on a downstream clustering task, achieving the best clustering performance on most of the collections.

papers.title: Synchrony, Affect, and Perceived Autonomy in Virtual Robot-Facilitated Anxiety Support Groups
papers.summary: Socially assistive robots could expand access to group-based mental health support when skilled human facilitators are unavailable. However, their effectiveness will depend on whether they foster productive interactions among participants. We examined dyadic head-movement synchrony among 96 participants across 18 virtual robot-facilitated anxiety support group sessions. A human-controlled virtual robot, via a Wizard-of-Oz (WoZ) system, facilitated all sessions. We found that stronger peak synchrony predicted lower post-session negative affect. In contrast, speakers who more often followed listeners' movements reported higher negative affect and state anxiety, demonstrating that synchrony strength and direction capture distinct interpersonal processes. Participants who believed the robot was autonomous showed more genuine synchrony and stronger peaks than those who believed it was human-operated; more negative attitudes toward robots also predicted greater synchrony. These findings support synchrony as an objective, behaviorally grounded measure for evaluating robot-facilitated groups and a potential signal for guiding future autonomous facilitators.

papers.title: Pathology Randomization for Synthetic Priors and Zero-Shot Detection
papers.summary: Hospital brain imaging archives hold a diverse array of pathology at sample sizes beyond prospective studies, particularly for underrepresented populations and diseases. To unlock uncurated clinical data and scale analysis, methods are needed to detect abnormalities across contrasts and resolutions. Synthetic data has provided robust, contrast-agnostic models for a variety of human neuroimaging tasks in healthy anatomy, but pathology detection and other tasks in clinical settings still require real patient data, contrast-specific models, or disease-specific generators. We propose PathoDraw, a generative model of brain MRI with pathology. A conditional distribution of lesions given the healthy anatomy is drawn into the label map before contrast-agnostic rendering, and a single network estimates healthy anatomy with exact signed intensity deviation of any input scan. The contrast-agnostic 3D UNet learns the healthy labels under the lesion and the signed deviation directly and identifies pathology via robust tissue statistics and learned features, despite no training on real pathology. We show zero-shot detection on public stroke, tumor, and white matter hyperintensity datasets as well as archived clinical data, spanning $T_1$w, FLAIR and $T_2$w at various resolutions under a recent unsupervised anomaly detection benchmark protocol. Our single model exceeds or performs comparably to contrast-specific anomaly detectors trained on real scans and keeps healthy anatomy intact. The same generator trains networks for super-resolution and for registration in the presence of pathology. Our model, robust across acquisition and disease, enables the use of uncurated, archived data for clinical analysis. Our code is available at https://github.com/agr78/Pathology-Randomizer.
papers.comment: 25 pages, 9 figures, 13 tables (8-page main text with appendices). Code: https://github.com/agr78/Pathology-Randomizer

papers.title: Beyond Bitwidth: Deployment-Constrained Mixed-Precision Quantization for Multilingual LLM Inference on NVIDIA Blackwell
papers.summary: Low-bit LLM quantization is useful only if a model preserves service-relevant accuracy, executes through supported GPU kernels, and meets measured memory and latency limits. We study Qwen3-8B on NVIDIA B200 with vLLM, including INT2/INT3, GPTQ, NVFP4, and mixed-precision configurations. We verify native packed execution and precision on all 144 fused linear modules and evaluate Korean, English, numerical, and reasoning quality under preregistered gates. Packed INT2 and INT3 execute, but all seven tested INT2 grids degenerate on generation. Isolated module-restoration effects are strongly non-additive; Korean and reasoning sensitivity rankings disagree, and a promising INT4/INT8 development candidate fails independent final evaluation. A configuration with 16-bit activations, 98 NVFP4 weight-only modules, 46 INT8 modules, and an INT8 output head passes all gates on the untouched FINAL-81 set (5,168 items): 5.917 GiB of weight-loading memory (limit 5.98), Korean teacher-correct retention 0.904 (gate 0.90), and TPOT ratio 0.939 relative to BF16. It improves paired accuracy over NVFP4 W4A4 by +1.4 percentage points (Bonferroni-adjusted interval [+0.2, +2.6]), compared with +3.4 points on the selection set. This comparison changes both activation precision and INT8 protection; exploratory analyses suggest that the activation change contributes substantially, but the isolated allocation effect is not established. Final checkpoints were not retained, and bitwise rebuild reproducibility remains unverified.

papers.title: Photonic Maxwells demon as an energy resource
papers.summary: We propose a new realization of Maxwells demon for photons and its use as an energy resource. The starting point is a multilayer dielectric mirror that transmits photons within a certain wavelength band but reflects photons at longer wavelengths, followed by a material that irreversibly converts the wavelength. A 3D box constructed from these one-way mirrors is a self-acting Maxwells demon for photons. The first case considered is a one-way mirror for visible photons, converting blue to red as an example. The next case is a one-way mirror that transmits visible light but reflects infrared light, followed by a perfect blackbody. We analyze a 3D box with such mirrors as walls to accumulate and store blackbody radiation. Applications include solar-powered thermal energy and solar-powered thermophotovoltaics. The latter case would combine the 3D box with an ultra-low bandgap semiconductor photovoltaic cell inside. In the ideal optical limit, radiation can enter the box but cannot return through the entrance channel after conversion, allowing repeated photon recycling and nearly complete optical utilization. This can in principle move the conversion efficiency toward the thermodynamic limit for solar-energy conversion, the Landsberg limit of 93.3%.

papers.title: It's My Turn! Interpretable Methods Reveal Developmental Differences from Mother-Child Conversational Dynamics
papers.summary: Understanding conversational interactions between mothers and children is an important challenge for computational behavioral modeling. Existing methods use traditional statistical approaches and subjective measures of conversational dynamics, without incorporating temporal or probabilistic modeling. We developed an interpretable computational framework that combines sequence analysis, information-theoretic measures, and Bayesian hierarchical modeling to characterize temporal conversational dynamics in parent-child play. We applied this framework to interactions from 94 mother-child dyads with two-year-old children. Sequence analysis revealed that dyads with lower language development (as defined by scores on the Bayley developmental test) exhibited more heterogeneous conversational organization and fewer serve-and-return exchanges than higher-development dyads, a reciprocal turn-taking pattern in which one partner initiates communication and the other responds. Mutual information analyses suggested differences in conversational predictability between lower- and higher-development dyads, although the bootstrap confidence intervals overlapped. Bayesian hierarchical models estimated temporal trajectories for maternal consecutive turns, child responses following maternal speech, and overlapping responses; HDIs showed that trajectories differed in whether they excluded 0, but there were no statistically credible differences between the Bayley groups. Overall, these results indicate that children with higher developmental scores have more organized and predictable communication styles, with more ``serve-and-return" patterns with their mothers. These results demonstrate that interpretable computational representations of conversational dynamics capture developmental differences beyond simple measures of speech quantity.

papers.title: Solver to System: LLM Reasoning Across Representations and Execution in Scientific Simulation
papers.summary: Simulators based on partial differential equations (PDEs) are widely used to model physical systems, but generating and interpreting PDE solver code with large language models (LLMs) remains challenging. Scientific simulation code is a useful testbed for LLM scientific reasoning because (1) one system can be represented by code, equations, natural language, and numerical trajectories and (2) code can execute successfully while implementing invalid physics. We introduce Solver2System, a dataset of PDE solvers with multiple representations, controlled corruptions, and lexical perturbations, to evaluate whether LLMs can recover the underlying physical system through (1) cross-representation consistency and (2) static and agentic detection of physical invalidity. Across eight open-weight models, LLMs systematically favor some representations when evidence conflicts, and lexical perturbations to code alter interpretation of other unchanged representations. Execution improves physical-validity judgments, but weaker agents can judge correctly without identifying the causal defect. Thus, LLMs may reach correct judgments despite inconsistent representation reconciliation or causal misdiagnosis.
papers.comment: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: Sim2Science: ML with Imperfect Scientific Models. 23 pages, 14 figures, 9 tables

papers.title: Structural balance in complex networks: from measurement to dynamics, emergence and implications
papers.summary: Structural balance theory, introduced in social psychology to describe how friendly and hostile ties organize into consistent patterns, has been reinterpreted through statistical physics and complex networks. In the classical formulation, a triad with positive or negative links, representing friendship and hostility, is balanced when the product of its signs is positive; a balanced network splits into at most two internally friendly, mutually hostile groups. This review synthesizes how the triadic formulation has been extended to a statistical-ensemble perspective in which balance is encoded by immanent three-body interactions described by a proper Hamiltonian, balanced configurations correspond to low-energy states, and balance measures serve as order parameters for transitions between consensus, polarization, and disorder. We organize the field into three sections: Measurement, Dynamics and Emergence, and Implications. In Measurement, we compare measures of structural balance and null models, and show that conclusions for a given system depend on the chosen measure and null model. In Dynamics and Emergence, we review deterministic and stochastic systems, including the gradient, Hamiltonian, and local triad models, and examine how noise, topology, and competing mechanisms determine whether balance emerges. In Implications, we survey consequences for belief formation, opinion contagion dynamics, polarization, international relations, and markets. Across domains, the evidence is strongest for local triadic stability and weakest for system-wide balance. Balance is not synonymous with harmony: balanced structures can reflect cohesion, polarization, or persistent conflict. Its empirical relevance is well supported in some reciprocal social systems, but remains less settled in biological and other complex networks.
papers.comment: 235 pages, 19 figures. Review article submitted to Physics Reports

papers.title: A Catalog of Young Stellar Objects in the Lagoon Nebula
papers.summary: M8, the Lagoon Nebula, has been known for more than 100 years as a region forming stars. It is (in projection) very close to if not in the Galactic Bulge. As a result, the source surface density is very high and source confusion is a substantial challenge. Because of the location, there have been many surveys that serendipitously observed M8, in addition to studies specifically targeting it. But to this point, there has been no effort to resolve source confusion across all the existing catalogs, spanning many different wavelengths, sensitivities, and spatial resolutions. We have done all of this source reconciliation, and present the merged catalog here. The net result is 3019 YSOs with largely photometric data and/or YSO selection from ~50 different origins, primarily ranging from $g$-band through 25 um, but with a significant number of X-ray sources, and some data of limited sensitivity out through 70-450 um. The catalog includes several flags that enable users to select, e.g., the YSOs that have been identified as young by the most studies, or the YSOs with the most multi-wavelength counterparts, or the ones with the clearest IR excesses. We use this catalog in a companion paper; it will also be of use in, e.g., future SPHEREx and Roman work.
papers.comment: Accepted by ApJS; figures degraded in resolution for arXiv

papers.title: OCCAM: Improved Single-Cell Representation Learning and Perturbation Effect Prediction
papers.summary: Predicting the effects of genetic perturbations requires models that generalize beyond observed cell contexts and gene combinations. We introduce Occam, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) framework for representation learning and perturbation-effect prediction. Occam combines cell representations learned through denoising with gene interaction, text, and protein-sequence features. It achieves the highest aggregate representation scores for perturbation information and cell-type preservation with batch integration. In cross-context few-shot prediction, a perturbation and a cell context are each observed during training, but never together. Occam better captures the measured response patterns for these unobserved combinations than four retrained competitors or direct transfer of the same perturbation's measured effects from other training cell lines. Without fine-tuning, Occam best distinguishes perturbations among the evaluated models and simple baselines in cell lines held out from predictor training, across seen and unseen assays. Predicting expression levels accurately in these settings remains challenging. For double perturbations, which target two genes simultaneously, Occam composes learned single-gene responses to better capture the combined response and reduce expression error compared with competing models and summed single-gene effects. These gains extend to both strongly additive and weakly additive responses. Together, these results support simple MLPs for cell representation learning and perturbation-effect prediction across contexts and gene combinations.

papers.title: Weight-space programming for tractor guidance controller: large language models natively write neural network weights that steer a real tractor
papers.summary: Weight-space programming is a process where a large language model reads and writes the weights of a neural network directly, guided by a natural language specification, without an optimiser or gradient descent. This study applies it to automatic tractor guidance, where a 253-parameter neural network steers along paths of lines and arcs and must be adapted when the machine changes, such as a slower steering actuator. GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 (also 5.2) edited the network for our research tractor using a small budget of simulated evaluations to repair a network trained for another tractor and write a controller into a network with zero weights. We compared them with an evolution strategy, gradient descent and pure pursuit in simulation and on the real tractor. Both models read the network and analysed the closed loop with control theory correctly, and Fable's repair without simulation succeeded only occasionally. With simulated feedback, both models repaired the trained network in single sessions and wrote a working controller from zero weights, whereas from zero the evolution strategy found none. The controllers written from zero were sparse and in a classical cascaded structure; one model edited the trained network while the other replaced it. Gradient descent reached higher accuracy with far more simulation, and all language model controllers steered the real tractor without intervention, with errors of the same order as pure pursuit. Language models can program the weights of a neural controller directly, much as control engineers design one. We call this Weight-Space Engineering.
papers.comment: 20 pages, 8 figures, 8 tables (1 in the appendices); includes a field test on a real tractor

papers.title: SCAN: Site-Aware Collaborative Privacy-Preserving Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for Neurological Disease Classification
papers.summary: Worldwide neuroimaging data could strengthen diagnostic foundation models, but privacy rules often prevent centralizing brain MRI scans. We present SCAN, a site-aware collaborative adaptation framework for Neurological Disease Classification that lets new sites adapt a 3D medical vision-language model (VLM) without retraining or sharing patient scans. Each site keeps exact class prototypes for local prediction and can share privacy-protected class summaries: norm-bounded sums and counts perturbed once with calibrated noise. Using 7,641 scans from 67 sites across 12 countries, covering Alzheimer's disease (AD), stroke, epilepsy and controls, we assess local adaptation, cross-site benefits, and effects on existing sites. At seven unseen sites, the frozen VLM's zero-shot AUCs were 0.833-0.945 for AD and stroke. Training-free local prototypes improved epilepsy AUC at three sites from 0.598/0.625/0.508 to 0.684/0.729/0.762 and AD AUC at one site from 0.833 to 0.863, nearly matching a classifier trained at each site (mean AUC 0.757 vs. 0.759). With differential privacy ($ε$ = 4), new sites contributed without materially reducing accuracy at existing sites (AUC change $\leq$0.2%), although gains from sharing were limited, and membership attacks performed near chance. SCAN offers hospitals a worldwide framework to adapt and share brain MRI VLMs without exchanging scans or retraining.

papers.title: Robust Decision Curve Analysis for Survival Risk Prediction Models in the Presence of Informative Censoring
papers.summary: Decision curve analysis (DCA) is recommended for evaluating the clinical utility of prediction models by quantifying net benefit (NB). Conventional NB estimators for survival outcomes rely on the assumption that censoring is non-informative, potentially yielding biased estimates and misleading decisions when this assumption is violated. We propose a robust estimator of survival NB using conditional inverse probability of censoring weighting (CIPCW). In simulation studies, we compared its performance against the conventional approach across censoring mechanisms, censoring model specifications, censoring rates, and decision thresholds, in terms of relative bias, relative root mean squared error (RMSE), and 90% confidence interval coverage. Under non-informative censoring, both estimators performed comparably, with relative bias below 1% and coverage close to the nominal level. Under informative censoring, conventional estimators underestimated the true NB by up to 58% with coverage as low as 1%, whereas the CIPCW estimator had a relative bias of at most 4%, coverage of at least 78% and consistently lower relative RMSE. As a case study, we illustrated its use in validating a breast cancer recurrence-free survival model to guide intensified adjuvant therapy in the German Breast Cancer Study Group (GBSG) cohort. Using the model was the best strategy at some clinically relevant thresholds, but accounting for potential informative censoring changed the best strategy to treating all patients, showing that informative censoring can change the conclusions drawn from DCA. When censoring may be informative, we recommend CIPCW-based NB estimation in DCA for survival outcomes.
papers.comment: 21 pages, 4 figures; Abdollah Safari and Tae Yoon Lee equally contributed

papers.title: Quantum Information Transfer in Molecular Polaritonic Networks: A Van Vleck Effective-Hamiltonian Approach
papers.summary: Achieving high-fidelity transfer of an arbitrary quantum state between spatially separated qubits is a central challenge for reliable quantum hardware. We address this question within a polaritonic framework by introducing Projected-Block Van Vleck Perturbation Theory (PB-VVPT). Based on quasidegenerate perturbation theory, this approach describes a molecular network coupled to an optical cavity and local phonons through a generalized Holstein--Tavis--Cummings Hamiltonian. Quantum information is encoded in a coherent superposition of exciton-cavity states, while phonons constitute a weakly coupled environment. In the nonadiabatic regime of weak exciton-phonon coupling, the method incorporates phonon-induced renormalization of polaritonic states and their dynamics while reducing the Hamiltonian to independent fixed-phonon-number sectors and coupled polaron-polariton subblocks. This structure provides efficient access to the coherence and population propagators governing quantum-state transfer without invoking a Markovian approximation. We benchmark the approach against exact dynamics for a molecular wheel network, considering both molecule-to-molecule and molecule-to-cavity transfer. PB-VVPT accurately reproduces short- and long-time transfer dynamics, including thermal decoherence and fidelity revivals consistent with non-Markovian memory effects, with prediction errors below $1\%$ over most of the simulated time intervals. This accuracy is achieved with an estimated diagonalization cost more than two orders of magnitude lower than that of the exact reference calculations. These results establish PB-VVPT as an accurate and computationally efficient approach to quantum information transfer in molecular polaritonic networks.

papers.title: Conserved Verdicts, Drifting Commitments: Identifying Harmful Overthinking
papers.summary: A reasoning model that has reached a correct answer can lose it by continuing to think. Deciding whether to stop means comparing two probabilities at the same point of a chain: that the answer the model would give if stopped now is correct (its commitment), and that the answer it will finish with is correct (its verdict). We show that the verdict alone, which is what final-correctness probes estimate, cannot make this comparison. As a forecast of a fixed outcome it has no predictable drift, whether continuing helps or hurts. The commitment-verdict gap equals the expected remaining change in answer quality and the accuracy gained by stopping. A second identity splits any accuracy-versus-budget curve into answer change within chains and change in which chains are still running. We measure both on MATH-500. At all 379 points where DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B holds a correct answer, selected without regard to how its chain ends, continuing loses 3.6 points on average (95% CI [2.2, 5.2]), and the loss concentrates in a few problems. In six reasoning models from three families, on MATH-500 and OlympiadBench and with budgets up to 16,384 tokens, declining accuracy curves come from which chains remain, while the chains still reasoning keep or improve their answers. An oracle stopping rule gains at most +1.8 and +2.5 points at 1.5B and 7B. The framework says what to measure before building a stopping rule.

papers.title: Benchmarking Deep Learning Models for Wheelchair Configuration Classification in Accessible Automated Vehicle Applications
papers.summary: Making automated vehicles accessible requires consideration of vulnerable road users, including wheelchair users. To offer a more tailored experience that supports independence for this group, vehicle design needs to accommodate the wide range of wheelchair configurations. However, wheelchairs are individualized, varying in frame geometry, propulsion, and visual appearance. Moreover, occupants or accessories may obscure visual cues. Existing mobility-aid datasets only label the presence of a wheelchair, rather than describing its specific configuration. To fill this gap, this paper introduces the Wheelchair Configuration Image Dataset (WCID), comprising 467 face-blurred images across 192 capture groups solely for evaluation. Each image is annotated with (i) a two-class label of manual or powered, (ii) a chair subtype, (iii) occupancy, viewpoint, setting, lighting, occlusion, propulsion, and control, with a 273-image validation split and 194-image test split. Three convolutional neural network backbones and a frozen vision-language probe are trained on an external image dataset and evaluated on WCID to measure cross-dataset generalization, while also testing robustness using Gaussian blur. Convolutional models do well on clean images, but performance drops under strong blur, leaving a gap before deployment. Code, split assignments, labels, trained weights, and the face-blurred images is available at: https://github.com/Mi3-Lab/MAID

papers.title: Complexity and precision in quantum associative retrieval
papers.summary: We show that efficient and high-precision quantum associative retrieval is possible with an exponential complexity advantage with respect to the classical brute force approach and with a polynomial capacity advantage with respect to classical neural network implementations for any number of patterns scaling polynomially in the number of qubits. Both classical neural and quantum associative memories store the patterns in a Hamiltonian; in the classical case the dynamics is irreversible relaxation toward attractors, in the quantum case it is unitary transformations generating an effective thermal distribution, followed by a measurement.

papers.title: A δ-adjusted Method for Tipping Point Sensitivity Analysis for a Binary Outcome with Missing Values
papers.summary: Missing data remain a persistent challenge in clinical trials despite preventive efforts. Handling missing data in clinical trials requires not only a primary analysis but also sensitivity analyses, as the underlying missingness assumptions are difficult to verify. The δ-adjusted analysis, which assesses the robustness of primary results by adding a sensitivity parameter δ for one or both treatment groups, has been widely used for continuous outcomes. Then, a set of tipping points which flip the significance of the primary analysis can be identified. However, there is no corresponding δ-adjusted method for binary variables. In this article, we propose a δ-adjusted method for binary variables that addresses this gap. This method assesses robustness by adding a sensitivity parameter to the logit function of the estimated response probability under the primary imputation approach and shares the same property as the δ-adjusted method for continuous variables. We applied this method to a clinical trial evaluating the treatment effect of tirzepatide 15 mg versus 5 mg on a composite binary endpoint. This method provides a principled sensitivity analysis framework for binary endpoints with broad applicability in clinical trials.

papers.title: HubEgo-100K: In-the-Wild Egocentric Video of Skilled Work for Robot Learning
papers.summary: Robot policies trained by imitation generalize poorly outside the environments and objects seen in training. Published data-scaling studies find that generalization grows with the diversity of training environments and objects rather than with more demonstrations per environment. Robot data is costly to collect across many environments, whereas egocentric human video can be recorded in the wild at scale; existing egocentric video, however, mostly shows daily-life activity and contains little skilled work in real workplaces. We present HubEgo-100K, a dataset built for diversity. This version of the paper covers the first release, v1.0: 10,124 hours of 1080p egocentric video with synchronized 100 Hz inertial (IMU) data from one head-mounted phone camera. In v1.0, 12,227 contributors record their own unscripted work in 15,548 environments (each one contributor's own setting of one type, such as their kitchen or workshop) across 11 setting types, 30 work categories, 56 task types and 35 action families, with 83% of hours in workplace settings. The release comprises 72,754 episodes with machine-generated action and language annotations, in LeRobot and MCAP formats under CC BY 4.0. We measure diversity along each axis, show that inside v1.0, with episodes in random order, new contributors and words keep appearing, and relate the measurements to published evidence on six data properties tied to policy performance, including hand visibility and inertial sensing. We also document collection, curation, privacy measures and data format, and provide a datasheet. Later versions of this paper will add benchmarks and cover further releases toward 100,000 hours.

papers.title: Higher-Order Interaction Reconstruction via Integral Physics-Informed Neural Networks
